title: Sidecar multiplexing for VPC telemetry segmentation and routed sampling
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Problem: Customers using Dedicated and Private deployments require that traces, metrics, and logs originating from co-located inference nodes never cross tenant boundaries and can be routed to either the customer-managed on-prem/VPC telemetry stack or Redwood-hosted observability endpoints. Existing approaches rely on a single collector process per host which complicates per-tenant isolation, sampled forwarding, and low-latency trace propagation.

Goal: Build a lightweight sidecar multiplexer (ingest-proxy) that lives alongside inference runtime pods/agents to: 1) securely tag and multiplex telemetry per-tenant, 2) apply configurable sampling and routing rules at the edge, 3) encrypt and forward to either customer endpoints (TLS/mTLS) or Redwood fallback endpoints, and 4) provide observability metrics and health checks for the local telemetry path.

Scope: design and implement sidecar multiplexer for traces and metrics (logs MVP deferred to a follow-up), include policy engine for tenant routing and sampled trace propagation, provide integration tests, performance benchmarks, rollout plan for Dedicated and VPC Private deployments, and console UI hints for per-deployment telemetry status.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar proxy container can be deployed as a mesh-sidecar or daemonset for on-prem nodes
Telemetry records (traces and metrics) are annotated with tenant_id and routed according to a policy table
Configurable sampling rules support rate-based and probabilistic sampling per-tenant
TLS/mTLS forwarding to customer endpoints with cert rotation support and KMS integration for keys
Unit and e2e tests validating tenant isolation (no cross-tenant spans/metrics delivered to wrong endpoint)
End-to-end latency overhead under 1.5ms p50 and <10% p99 for hot-path trace propagation at baseline load
Automated health metrics exported to Redwood console (sidecar_up, queue_depth, per-tenant_drop_rate)
Docs and migration notes for Dedicated and Private customers with step-by-step configuration and fallback guidance
notes: Architectural approach: sidecar performs demux based on local tenant header or pod annotation, uses a small in-memory routing table that is updated from the control plane via signed config bundles.
Sampling rules stored as versioned bundles; control plane will push when customer changes sampling or routing policies.
Considerations around zero-trust: sidecar will validate customer TLS endpoints and perform mTLS when customer provides certs; fallback to Redwood endpoints requires explicit allowlist.
Performance plan: microbenchmarks in lab with 8x A100 nodes and synthetic workload; measure CPU overhead, memory, and added latency across common sequence lengths.
Migration/backwards compatibility: if sidecar is unavailable, runtime should fallback to direct local forwarding to host agent but be blocked for tenants marked 'strict isolation'.
